newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile Disputada's copper mine seen hit by snowfall.
newsitem.headline: Chile Disputada's copper mine seen hit by snowfall.

text.p: Work at one of two mines owned by Exxon Corp's Disputada de Las Condes copper producer may have been stopped by heavy snow, a spokesman for the mine said.
But the mine, the Los Bronces open pit, was using stockpiles to keep the concentrator plant going, while Disputada's larger mine, El Soldado, was working normally, said spokesman Guillermo Garcia.

He said communications with the mine were bad because of the weather but that heavy snow may have stopped work inside Los Bronces mine, as usually happens during the winter months at the mine lying high in the Andes northeast of Santiago.
"It's possible that the mine itself is not working because of the excess of snow," said Garcia. "The SAG mills (in the concentrator) are working with stockpiles."
"We've got a lot of snow but we're used to operating with snow. This is quite a normal occurrence, and we're using the stockpiles because that's what stockpiles are for," he said.

Los Bronces accounts for about 80,000 tonnes of Disputada's 200,000 tonnes annual copper output and the rest is from El Soldado. Ore from Los Bronces runs through the crusher and mills at the mine and then runs down a 56-km underground pipeline to the flotation plant near Peldehue, at a much lower elevation, said Garcia.

El Soldado, about 130 km north of Santiago in an area that has been hit by floods since the weekend, was operating normally but workers were trying to get rid of excess water in the mine after heavy rains since Thursday, said Garcia.
"There is a lot of water and we're making efforts to channel it out," he said.
